build_order_basis: Wave 1 starts with fixed serial arms that can plausibly reuse the existing arm_serial_dls family, beginning with Franka Panda, then Kinova Gen3 and xArm7, followed by the other fixed arms.
Wave 2 prioritizes the articulated hand after the fixed-arm package pattern is understood; Unitree G1 and Barkour remain optional backup research outside the formal mainline.
Wave 3 covers the mobile and bimanual manipulators, which require broader coordination interfaces.

The official-source review found a compatible pinned BarkourJoystick training environment in MuJoCo Playground v0.0.5 but no official pretrained vB checkpoint in the inspected repositories or release assets. It records the retained 465-value observation-history actor, 12-value action mapping, observation normalizer, exact 20 ms to canonical 1 ms CPU bridge, completed flat calibration gate, material dynamics mismatch, and the continuing need for specialist obstacle policies plus a reference-only course planner. This is bounded research and calibration evidence, not package-wide task-success or runnable evidence.

A locally trained 100,270,080-step BarkourJoystick actor, including its observation normalizer, matched exported NumPy inference within 3.10e-06 and completed the unmodified canonical CPU bridge using only data.ctrl and 20 one-millisecond MuJoCo steps per action. The five-second stand and all eight 0.4 m/s direction checks completed without falls; all nine videos decode and representative cases were visually checked. This closes only the flat-controller calibration gate, not private cases, trusted Harness verdicts, obstacle coverage, a package-wide positive control, or runnable status.

The retained actor, observation normalizer, pinned source/runtime/training metadata, and exact 20-by-1-ms canonical CPU bridge are self-contained under the robot package and trusted skeleton resource. Focused tests reproduce a five-second upright stand and all eight flat 0.4 m/s directions without falls. The wrapper has no task dispatch, private definitions, scene loading, simulator reset, verdict logic, or reference/driver.py entrypoint; specialist policies and a complete package-wide positive-control driver remain missing.

The public package now exposes a task-neutral Barkour position-policy skeleton backed by the retained actor and observation normalizer in the trusted runtime package. A skeleton-assisted probe stages that resource without reference or private files, and a candidate-worker check executes 200 canonical MuJoCo steps through data.ctrl. This closes the flat position-policy skeleton gap only, not obstacle specialists, a package-wide positive control, or runnable status.

locally_observed_source_material.observation: The canonical research-only package contains the pinned Menagerie standard 29-actuator G1 asset closure. Its scene loads in MuJoCo 3.3.6 with a free base, 29 hinge joints and matching position actuators, four named sites, four IMU sensors, the stand keyframe, finite reset contacts, and real actuator-stepping liveness; this is asset evidence, not humanoid-control or task-success evidence.

The canonical morphology records the standard G1 29-DoF model identity, exact joint and actuator maps, limits, gains, joint-level force limits, free-base observations, foot and IMU sites, reset facts, and pinned source lineage without claiming runnable status.

The canonical G1 public snapshot records four pinned primary sources: the exact Menagerie morphology, HumanoidBench code and paper, RoboCup Humanoid League 2025 rules, and Safety Gym implementation. These records support the 20 public contracts without claiming controller or task success.

The canonical G1 public snapshot contains 20 distinct source-backed task contracts and 20 machine-expressible scoring clauses: thirteen HumanoidBench tasks, five RoboCup challenges, and two Safety Gym tasks. Each records its canonical 29-actuator morphology adaptation, and focused validation loads the exact MuJoCo scene. This is public contract evidence only, not private evaluation, complete task success, or runnable evidence.

The task-neutral G1 skeleton binds the exact 29 joint-position actuators, enforces model and control ranges, exposes public joint/base/site observations, and advances the canonical MuJoCo session without direct qpos or qvel writes. It is low-level control inventory only, not a balance, locomotion, reward, or reference policy.

The self-contained Unitree mjlab scene pins the official G1 training collision model, 0.005 s physics timestep, 29 position actuators, source gains, damping, effort limits, armatures, and HOME keyframe at repository revision 1425b15f73bd4095f0df53709d7c389c3eb9e790. All 35 referenced meshes are byte-identical to the package's retained Menagerie closure.

The Apache-2.0 Unitree velocity policy is retained as a pure NumPy 98-512-256-128-29 ELU network with its source normalizer and exact 29-joint action map. Focused Direct-MuJoCo positive controls held the HOME pose for 4 s with less than 0.04 m planar drift and walked forward for 4 s at a 0.3 m/s command with more than 0.9 m progress, upright projection above 0.99, and no direct qpos or qvel writes. This proves only the task-neutral stand/velocity foundation, not the complete 20-task reference route.
